answer: A proof-of-space protocol limits Sybil attacks by forcing agents to allocate hard drive sectors to cryptographic plots. The cedar registry verifies spatial proofs across an indexed storage vine, linking identity to non-volatile disk capacity. To spawn identities, an attacker must acquire scarce physical storage hardware instead of virtualizing nodes. A violet auditor challenges sector integrity over time. However, this design favors industrial storage farms and penalizes lightweight agents.
